title: Access translation wave controller and admin verification guide
creator: Sofia Martinez
description: Purpose: Define a conservative, observable, and reversible plan to translate tenant and principal permissions from RBAC v1 to RBAC v2. This ticket covers the orchestration controller (wave controller) that coordinates translation waves, the admin verification checklist and tooling for operators, and the customer-facing comms and opt-in patterns. Scope includes dual-write plumbing, incremental backfills, canary preview orgs, audit forwarding validation, SSO/SAML role map verification, and runbook automation. Non-goals: changes to permission semantics, UI role definitions, or long-term storage format beyond what is required for migration compatibility.
acceptance_criteria: Wave controller can schedule and pause translation waves by org and by tenant label
Dual-write path established and validated (writes to v1 and v2) with a data loss safety net
Backfill job supports windowed retries, progress checkpoints, and resumability
Admin verification checklist achieves operator sign-off for 5 canary orgs before wider rollout
Audit logs for every translated permission event are emitted, immutable, and visible in Grafana dashboard
Automated SSO/SAML mappings test harness runs against mapped assertions and reports mismatches
Customer comms templates and opt-in flow implemented and approved by Legal and PM
tasks: Design wave controller CRD and control plane APIs
Implement dual-write middleware with sampling and telemetry
Build backfill worker with checkpointed queue consumer
Create admin verification UI page and CLI helper for operator checks
Integrate audit forwarder to immutable event stream and test exports
Add SSO mapping test harness and synthetic assertions generator
Prepare customer communications, release notes, and org opt-in flow
Create runbook for abort and rollback with clear health-check thresholds
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Divergent writes between v1 and v2 creating inconsistent permission state; Mitigation: dual-write with sampled reads and a divergence detector that pauses waves on >0.05% divergence
Risk: Backfill throughput saturates DB; Mitigation: rate-limited backfill, prioritized windows, and maintenance-mode leases
Risk: SSO mapping differences cause access regressions; Mitigation: preflight SAML assertion replay across mapped roles and org-level opt-in gating
Risk: Audit exports missed during cutover; Mitigation: duplicate audit stream to write-ahead log and verify parity before cutover
Risk: Customer confusion around opt-in; Mitigation: targeted communications, in-console banner with rollback path, and support playbook
rollout_phases: Phase 0 - Prep: schema compatibility checks, telemetry hooks, and runbook dry-run (internal)
Phase 1 - Dual-write & Sampling: enable dual-write for a small set of internal orgs with divergence telemetry
Phase 2 - Canary Preview Waves: run translation on 5 customer orgs (opt-in) and execute full verification checklist
Phase 3 - Incremental Backfills: launch wave controller to run batched backfills by tenant size (small -> medium -> large)
Phase 4 - Cutover Window: coordinated cutover where reads point to v2, with immediate fallback to v1 for critical errors
Phase 5 - Post-cutover Observability: 72-hour elevated telemetry retention, audit validation, and a 7-day reconciliation job
comms_plan: Pre-announcement to customers with timeline and FAQ (T-minus 21 days)
Targeted invites for canary preview orgs and opt-in instructions (T-minus 14 days)
In-console banner and support-runbook links during canary windows
Cutover notice 48 hours before a customer's cutover window and immediate post-cutover health summary
Post-cutover postmortem and opportunity to opt-out via support ticket for 7 days
audit_requirements: All translation events must emit audit entries with actor, timestamp, before/after permission deltas, and wave_id
Audit stream must be forwarded to immutable storage with retention >= 365 days
Export parity check between v1 and v2 audit streams must be run pre- and post-cutover
